custody.record: Legacy of Mandalore
custody.note: Beats Saxon on the ice using Ezra's lightsaber and takes it back.

custody.record: Heroes of Mandalore
custody.note: Accepts it once the clans pledge to follow her.

custody.record: Chapter 23: The Spies
custody.note: Bo-Katan yields it hoping to halt the Purge; the Empire keeps killing anyway.

custody.record: Chapter 16: The Rescue
custody.note: Defeats Gideon with his beskar spear; Bo-Katan will not take it as a gift.

custody.record: Chapter 18: The Mines of Mandalore
custody.note: Whips it off the ground to kill the cyborg holding Din, then hands it back.

custody.record: Chapter 18: The Mines of Mandalore
custody.note: Later argues that her rescue of him makes the blade rightly hers.

custody.record: Chapter 22: Guns for Hire
custody.note: Din presents it before the Mandalorian fleet, which accepts her as its bearer.

artifacts.conflict: Star Wars: Timelines places both Tarre Vizsla's induction as a child and the saber's creation around 1050 BBY; he made it later as a Knight, so the creation date is approximate.

artifacts.name: The Skywalker lightsaber

fate.text: Buried beside Leia's saber at the old Lars farm on Tatooine.

artifacts.summary: Anakin's blue saber from his Clone Wars campaigns. On Mustafar Obi-Wan takes it, later giving it to Luke, who loses it at Cloud City. Decades later it calls to Rey from Maz Kanata's vault, splits in two, is mended, and is finally laid to rest on Tatooine.

custody.note: Made to replace the first saber he lost on Geonosis.
sources: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones
Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales 1

custody.record: Hostage Crisis
custody.note: Anakin leaves it with her as a token of trust; she hides it through Cad Bane's raid.

custody.record: Hostage Crisis

custody.note: Pulls it from a Sith altar with Maul, later pries it from the obelisk with Kanan.

custody.record: Steps Into Shadow
custody.note: Takes charge of it after catching Ezra studying its dark lessons.

custody.record: Steps Into Shadow
custody.note: Stashes it in a cave guarded by krykna spiders.

custody.record: The Holocrons of Fate
custody.note: Fetches it from the krykna tunnels to ransom his captured friends.

custody.record: The Holocrons of Fate
custody.note: Fused with Kanan's holocron at Maul's demand; the explosion damages both.
The cracked holocron sits at Chopper Base; Maul keeps a shard to reach Ezra's mind.

artifacts.name: The sacred Jedi texts

made.yText: undated; from the Jedi Order's dawn
made.tText: undated; from the Jedi Order's dawn

fate.text: Kept by Rey once Palpatine falls, as of the latest canon.

artifacts.summary: Eight ancient books and scrolls dating to the Jedi Order's beginnings. Luke gathers them across the galaxy and shelves them inside a hollow tree on Ahch-To; Rey quietly takes them aboard the Falcon and uses their lessons to mend her saber and chart a way to Exegol.

custody.note: Written by early sages such as Kli the Elder and Lyr Farseeker.
sources: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: A Junior Novel

custody.note: A Jedi historian who preserves the two Aionomica volumes; a forged third surfaces c. 319 BBY.
sources: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

custody.note: Starts with a book from Gazian's Living Sea, adds the Rammahgon from Ossus, and annotates them.
sources: Star Wars: The Last Jedi: The Visual Dictionary
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

custody.record: Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi
custody.note: Slips them onto the Falcon before Luke tries to burn the library tree.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi
Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

made.yText: undated; first held by the Eye of Webbish Bog
made.tText: undated; first held by the Eye of Webbish Bog

fate.text: Guides Rey to Exegol and gives the Resistance the route.

artifacts.summary: One of two Sith wayfinders that chart the hidden route to Exegol. Mustafar's Eye of Webbish Bog gives it to Vader, who later returns it to the Eye's keeping on Mustafar. Kylo Ren takes it decades later, and Rey uses it to reach Palpatine.

custody.note: A Mustafar entity that holds the device before Vader arrives.
As Vader he uses it to learn what his master is doing on Exegol.
Vader leaves it in the Eye's care; Alazmec cultists guard Fortress Vader's ruins.
sources: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

custody.record: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
custody.note: Cuts through the cultists; the Eye yields it and he flies to Exegol.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition

custody.record: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
custody.note: Salvages it from Kylo's burning TIE whisper on Ahch-To.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary
Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

made.tText: undated; aboard the second Death Star by 4 ABY

artifacts.summary: Palpatine's own wayfinder, kept in the Imperial Vault next to his private throne room on the unfinished second Death Star. It survives the station's fall in the wreckage on Kef Bir until Rey finds it; Kylo Ren crushes it to force her to go to Exegol with him.

custody.note: Stored in his throne room's vault on the new battle station.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

custody.note: Survives the station's destruction inside the wreck on Endor's ocean moon.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

custody.record: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
custody.note: Finds it off the ruined throne room; a dark vision makes her drop it.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

custody.note: Picks it up, then crushes it so she must travel to Exegol with him.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

artifacts.name: The map to Peridea (Arcana Star Map)

fate.text: Cut apart by Baylan Skoll's lightsaber on Seatos.

artifacts.summary: A golden orb from a Nightsister temple on Arcana that projects the path to Peridea. Ahsoka finds it, Sabine unlocks it, and Shin Hati's droid takes it for Morgan Elsbeth; on Seatos, Sabine hands it to Baylan Skoll for passage to Ezra, and Baylan destroys it.

custody.note: Sealed in a temple built by Morgan Elsbeth's Nightsister ancestors.

custody.record: Part One: Master and Apprentice
custody.note: Recovers it from the temple and fights off assassin droids.

custody.record: Part One: Master and Apprentice
custody.note: Takes it home against Ahsoka's orders and solves its puzzle.

custody.record: Part One: Master and Apprentice
custody.note: An HK assassin droid grabs it while Hati runs Sabine through.

custody.record: Part Two: Toil and Trouble
custody.note: Baylan sets it on a pedestal on Seatos, and Elsbeth reads the pathway from it.

custody.record: Part Four: Fallen Jedi
custody.note: Grabs the orb to break the projection, burning her hand.

custody.record: Part Four: Fallen Jedi
custody.note: Told to destroy it, she holds it at blaster point instead.

custody.record: Part Four: Fallen Jedi
custody.note: Sabine hands it over for passage to Ezra; he completes the course, then destroys it.

anomalies.title: The Republic's founding: 25,000 or 20,000 BBY
anomalies.summary: The reference works put the Republic's birth five thousand years apart. The Star Wars Book counts back about 25,000 years, Star Wars: Timelines gives about 20,000, and Palpatine speaks of a Republic a thousand years old. Wookieepedia's timeline and its Republic article do not settle on the same answer.

accounts.claim: The Republic forms about 25,000 years before the Battle of Yavin.
accounts.source: The Star Wars Book

accounts.claim: The founding falls around 20,000 BBY.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Timelines, as Wookieepedia's Republic article cites it

accounts.claim: The Republic has stood for a thousand years and must not be split in two.
accounts.source: Palpatine, Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones

anomalies.resolution: Wookieepedia's timeline uses c. 25,000 BBY; its Republic article gives the whole 25,000–20,000 window. Palpatine's thousand years is read as the age of the modern Republic, rebuilt after the Jedi–Sith war around 1032 BBY. No source fixes one year.
sources: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones

anomalies.title: The Council rewrites Revan
anomalies.summary: In the Legends continuity, the Sith Lord Revan is betrayed by his apprentice Malak and captured by Jedi, near death. The Council does not try him. It erases his memory and sends him out believing he is a Republic trooper, hoping he will lead them to the Star Forge. The Jedi's own explanations of why he fell also disagree.

accounts.claim: Revan's mind is wiped, and he wakes as an ordinary soldier aboard the Endar Spire.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic

accounts.claim: Revan and Malak turned after exploring the ancient ruins on Dantooine.
accounts.source: The Jedi Council, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic

accounts.claim: Revan's fall began before the Mandalorian Wars.
accounts.source: Vrook Lamar, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic

accounts.claim: The Sith Emperor broke both men in the Unknown Regions and sent them back as his servants.
accounts.source: The Old Republic: Revan

anomalies.resolution: The novel's answer became the Legends record of why they fell. The Council never undoes the wipe; Revan learns who he was during the war and recovers the rest of his memory years later.
sources: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic

anomalies.title: The Darksaber's date, read two ways
anomalies.summary: Star Wars: Timelines gives a single date for Tarre Vizsla, about 1050 BBY. Wookieepedia's Darksaber article reads it as the year he made the black blade; its Tarre Vizsla article reads it as the year he joined the Jedi Order as a boy. If the second is right, the saber came years later, once he was a Knight.

accounts.claim: Tarre Vizsla creates the Darksaber around 1050 BBY.
accounts.source: Wookieepedia's Darksaber article, reading Star Wars: Timelines

accounts.claim: Around 1050 BBY the boy Tarre joins the Jedi Order; he builds the saber later, as a Knight.
accounts.source: Wookieepedia's Tarre Vizsla article, reading Star Wars: Timelines

accounts.claim: By legend the blade was made more than a thousand years ago by the first Mandalorian Jedi.
accounts.source: Fenn Rau, Trials of the Darksaber

anomalies.resolution: Open. One circa date is pinned to two different moments, and Fenn Rau's 'more than a thousand years' fits either. The chronicle dates the forging to c. 1050 BBY and carries the other reading as a flag.

anomalies.title: How old is the Jedi Temple?
anomalies.summary: Star Wars: Timelines dates the modern Temple on Coruscant to about 1032 BBY, when the Four Masters raise it after the Jedi–Sith war. Star Wars: Complete Locations says it was rebuilt some two thousand years before the Empire, with pieces of an earlier temple set into its base. The two dates sit about a millennium apart.

accounts.claim: The Four Masters build the modern Temple around 1032 BBY.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Timelines

accounts.claim: The Temple was rebuilt about two thousand years before the Empire, over remnants of an older one.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)

accounts.claim: The Temple takes shape slowly, over centuries, on top of a buried Sith shrine.
accounts.source: Nexus of Power

anomalies.resolution: Both dates stand in Wookieepedia's article, which describes a Temple rebuilt and expanded many times. A long building history can hold both, but no source says which rebuilding each date means. The chronicle uses c. 1032 BBY.

anomalies.title: When the Massassi died out
anomalies.summary: The builders of Yavin 4's temples are long gone when the Rebellion moves in, but the sources disagree on how long. Star Wars: Timelines places their extinction around 1000 BBY. In Doctor Aphra, set around the Battle of Yavin, Aphra says they have been extinct for millennia.

accounts.claim: The Massassi die out around 1000 BBY.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Timelines

accounts.claim: The Massassi died out thousands of years ago.
accounts.source: Chelli Aphra, Doctor Aphra (2016) 3

anomalies.resolution: Unresolved. Wookieepedia's Massassi article carries a conflict notice and follows the comic's 'millennia'; the chronicle keeps Timelines' c. 1000 BBY. A single millennium is the most the two can share.

anomalies.title: Two thousand-year counts for Kijimi
anomalies.summary: Two sources say the Dai Bendu came to Kijimi about a thousand years ago, but they count from different moments. Poe Dameron: Free Fall speaks from 18 ABY, which gives about 982 BBY for the city. The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary counts back from Kijimi's destruction in 35 ABY, which gives about 965 BBY for the monastery.

accounts.claim: Kijimi City has stood for a thousand years when Poe arrives with the Spice Runners.
accounts.source: Poe Dameron: Free Fall

accounts.claim: The Dai Bendu monastery was built a thousand years before the planet was destroyed.
accounts.source: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

anomalies.resolution: Both are round numbers, seventeen years apart. Wookieepedia's monastery article uses c. 965 BBY; the chronicle keeps c. 982 BBY for the first settlement.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

anomalies.title: Maz Kanata's thousand years
anomalies.summary: Han Solo tells Rey and Finn that Maz has run her Takodana watering hole for a thousand years, which would put her arrival near 966 BBY. Star Wars: Timelines dates her settling there to about 873 BBY, close to a century later.

accounts.claim: Maz has kept her watering hole on Takodana for a thousand years.
accounts.source: Han Solo, Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens

accounts.claim: Maz makes Takodana her home around 873 BBY.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Timelines

anomalies.resolution: The chronicle follows Timelines. Han's figure reads as a round number, but no source reconciles the two.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens

anomalies.title: Dagan Gera's two hundred twenty-four years
anomalies.summary: Dagan Gera is sealed in a bacta tank on Koboh after the Nihil overrun Tanalorr, and Cal Kestis frees him in 9 BBY, 224 years later by Wookieepedia's count. That count puts his sealing in 233 BBY, a year before the attack that led to it, which is dated 232 BBY.

accounts.claim: The Nihil overrun Tanalorr some time after the Great Hyperspace Disaster; the attack is dated 232 BBY.
accounts.source: Wookieepedia's Attack on Tanalorr article, from Lucasfilm Publishing's 2023 panel

accounts.claim: Gera is freed in 9 BBY after 224 years in stasis.
accounts.source: Wookieepedia's Dagan Gera article

accounts.claim: Gera is sealed away only after Tanalorr falls and he turns on his fellow Jedi.
accounts.source: Star Wars Jedi: Survivor

anomalies.resolution: An arithmetic mismatch between two articles, off by a year. The game gives no exact figure that forces either. The chronicle keeps 232 BBY for the attack.
sources: Star Wars: The High Republic: Chronicles of the Jedi

anomalies.title: The Brendok fire, told from each side
anomalies.summary: Four Jedi come to Brendok to test twin girls raised by a coven of witches, and by morning the coven is dead and its fortress burned. Mae grows up sure the Jedi murdered her family. Osha believes Mae set the fire and died in it. The Jedi agree to report the night from a certain point of view.

accounts.claim: The four Jedi invaded their home, and everyone died because of them.
accounts.source: Mae, The Acolyte (episode)

accounts.claim: Mae started the fire, and the deaths that night are on her.
accounts.source: Osha, Destiny (The Acolyte); The Acolyte (episode)

accounts.claim: Mae's fire was an accident; Sol killed Aniseya mistaking her magic for an attack; the witches died when Indara broke their hold on Kelnacca.
accounts.source: Choice

accounts.claim: The four Jedi agree to leave out whatever reflects badly on them or harms Osha's chances.
accounts.source: Choice

anomalies.resolution: Choice gives the fullest picture, and in 132 BBY Sol finally admits killing Aniseya. The report the four Jedi agreed on had left that out; Vernestra's account after his death becomes the next official version.

anomalies.title: Vernestra's report: blame the dead Master
anomalies.summary: With Master Sol dead on Brendok and a senator pressing for an outside review of the Jedi, Vernestra Rwoh tells the Chancellor the deaths were the work of one flawed Master, who took his own life at the scene. The dark-side killer behind the Khofar massacre goes unmentioned. Osha has left with him, and he has wiped Mae's memory.

accounts.claim: The Brendok deaths were one flawed man's doing, and he killed himself where it happened.
accounts.source: Vernestra Rwoh, The Acolyte (episode)

accounts.claim: Vernestra is running a murder inquiry inside the Order without reporting it to the Senate.
accounts.source: Senator Rayencourt, The Acolyte (episode)

accounts.claim: The Stranger kills the Jedi on Khofar; Osha kills Sol and leaves as the Stranger's apprentice.
accounts.source: Night; The Acolyte (episode)

accounts.claim: Mae's memory is wiped; she recalls only a fire and a man who killed her mother.
accounts.source: The Acolyte (episode)

anomalies.resolution: The Senate hears the Order's version, and the series ends before anyone tests it. No later work has returned to the report.

anomalies.title: A senator thirteen years early
anomalies.summary: Complete Locations says Naboo's senator, Palpatine, attended the opening of Theed's plasma generator, and Nexus of Power dates the plant to 65 BBY. But Star Wars: Timelines has Palpatine elected senator only in 52 BBY. Either he attended in some other role, or one of the dates is wrong.

accounts.claim: The generator is built in 65 BBY by a Naboo venture with Damask Holdings.
accounts.source: Nexus of Power

accounts.claim: Senator Palpatine attends the opening and takes an interest in its deep-pit design.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)

accounts.claim: Palpatine is elected Senator of Naboo in 52 BBY.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Timelines

anomalies.resolution: Unreconciled. Wookieepedia keeps all three statements and marks none as wrong. The chronicle keeps 65 BBY for the plant and 52 BBY for the election.

anomalies.title: Was Anakin born on Tatooine?
anomalies.summary: Tatooine is Anakin's home, but the record of his birth is thin: an enslaved mother, no father, owners who trade them away. The Star Wars Book names Tatooine as his birthplace. Darth Vader: Sith Lord says the records disagree, and that some have him brought to Tatooine as a small child.

accounts.claim: Anakin is born on Tatooine.
accounts.source: The Star Wars Book

accounts.claim: Records differ; some say he came to Tatooine with his mother when very young.
accounts.source: Darth Vader: Sith Lord

accounts.claim: Shmi bears him with no father, and the two are slaves on Tatooine when the Jedi find them.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace

anomalies.resolution: Wookieepedia lists Tatooine as his birthplace but marks it disputed. The chronicle follows The Star Wars Book; Tatooine is his homeworld either way.
sources: Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace

anomalies.title: How Sidious took Maul
anomalies.summary: All accounts agree Sidious took the Zabrak boy from Dathomir around 40 BBY. How depends on the teller. Talzin calls it theft. A legend in Myths & Fables has her give him up under pressure before Sidious picks him at a Selection. Maul's own memories, shown decades later, match neither, and his voice actor hints that is deliberate.

accounts.claim: Sidious broke his promise to Talzin and stole her son.
accounts.source: Talzin, Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 3

accounts.claim: Sidious makes Talzin hand Maul to a keeper; after months of abuse, Maul wins Sidious's eye at a Selection.
accounts.source: An Unwilling Apprentice, a legend in Myths & Fables

accounts.claim: Maul leaves with Sidious believing he has no choice, while Savage Opress pleads with him to stay.
accounts.source: Maul's memories, Chapter 8: The Creeping Fear

accounts.claim: Nothing in that vision matches the earlier shows, and viewers should ask why.
accounts.source: Sam Witwer, Maul's voice actor (2026)

anomalies.resolution: Open by design. Talzin's version comes from a canon comic, the Selection story is told as a legend, and Maul's memory is framed as unreliable. Wookieepedia presents all three without choosing.

anomalies.title: Palpatine's tale of Darth Plagueis
anomalies.summary: At the opera, Palpatine tells Anakin of a Sith Lord who could bend midi-chlorians into making life and could spare loved ones from dying, until his apprentice murdered him as he slept. The teller is that apprentice; the tale is bait. How much is true, when Plagueis died, and whether he made Anakin all stay disputed.

accounts.claim: Plagueis could make midi-chlorians create life and could save others from death; his apprentice killed him as he slept.
accounts.source: Palpatine, Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith

accounts.claim: There was no father; Shmi carried and bore Anakin and cannot explain it.
accounts.source: Shmi Skywalker, Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace

accounts.claim: Palpatine's story of Plagueis's powers was a lie; Anakin was made by the will of the Force.
accounts.source: George Lucas, The Star Wars Archives: Episodes I–III, 1999–2005

accounts.claim: An early story treatment had Sidious claim he willed Anakin's conception himself; Lucas cut it.
accounts.source: The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith

anomalies.resolution: Later canon treats Plagueis's powers as real, and a Databank entry and a reference book disagree on whether he died before or after Sidious took Maul. The films never answer the Anakin question; Lucas's own answer is the Force itself.
sources: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith
Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace
The Star Wars Archives: Episodes I–III, 1999–2005
The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition

anomalies.title: When Sifo-Dyas ordered the clones
anomalies.summary: On Kamino in 22 BBY, the Kaminoans tell Obi-Wan the army was ordered almost ten years before, which points to about 32 BBY, the year of the Naboo crisis. Star Wars: Timelines and Star Wars Insider 206 put the order in 33 BBY. The gap decides whether the order came a year before the Naboo crisis or during it.

accounts.claim: Sifo-Dyas placed the order almost ten years ago.
accounts.source: Lama Su, Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones

accounts.claim: Sifo-Dyas secretly commissions the army from Kamino in 33 BBY, without the Council knowing.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Timelines; Star Wars Insider 206

anomalies.resolution: The chronicle and Wookieepedia follow 33 BBY. The film's 'almost ten years' points to 32 BBY and is left unreconciled.
sources: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones

anomalies.title: The Sith, extinct for a millennium
anomalies.summary: When Qui-Gon reports a Sith warrior on Tatooine, the Jedi Council answers that the Sith have been gone for a thousand years. They were hiding, not gone. Since Darth Bane's Rule of Two, one master and one apprentice have kept the order alive out of the Jedi's sight, and the master now sits in the Senate.

accounts.claim: The Sith have been extinct for a millennium.
accounts.source: Ki-Adi-Mundi, Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace

accounts.claim: There are always two Sith, a master and an apprentice, so Maul's death leaves one of them still at large.
accounts.source: Yoda and Mace Windu, Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace

accounts.claim: Darth Bane allowed only two Sith at a time, hidden in the shadows while his plan worked toward the Jedi's ruin.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Timelines

anomalies.resolution: The Sith were never extinct, only hidden, and the Council's belief was the cover Sidious relied on. The Jedi learn who the master is in 19 BBY, too late.
sources: Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace

anomalies.title: Kamino missing from the Jedi Archives
anomalies.yText: c. 32 BBY; found missing in 22 BBY
anomalies.summary: Tracing a bounty hunter in 22 BBY, Obi-Wan searches the Jedi Archives for Kamino and finds empty space where gravity says a planet must be. Jocasta Nu insists the records are complete; one of Yoda's younglings sees that someone erased it. The film never says who; Tales of the Jedi answers twenty years later: Dooku, turning to Sidious.

accounts.claim: If a planet is not in the Archives, it does not exist.
accounts.source: Jocasta Nu, Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones

accounts.claim: Gravity pulls the nearby stars toward an empty spot, so someone must have erased the planet from the Archives.
accounts.source: Obi-Wan and a youngling, with Yoda agreeing, Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones

accounts.claim: Dooku deletes Kamino's records from the Archives.
accounts.source: The Sith Lord

accounts.claim: Lucas meant to solve the mystery in Revenge of the Sith but cut it to keep the story on Anakin.
accounts.source: George Lucas, Revenge of the Sith DVD commentary

anomalies.resolution: Answered on screen in 2022: Dooku did it, around the time of the Naboo crisis. The Jedi later uncover Tyranus's part in the clone army, but no work shows them learning who emptied the file.
sources: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones
Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith
anomalies.tText: c. 32 BBY; found missing in 22 BBY

anomalies.title: Maul, cut in half, lives on
anomalies.summary: The Phantom Menace ends with Obi-Wan slicing Maul in half and the halves falling down a reactor shaft, and for thirteen years that was his end. In 2012 The Clone Wars revealed he had survived on hatred, living as a maddened scavenger on a junk world until his brother Savage found him. Rebels, Solo and his own series followed.

accounts.claim: Obi-Wan cuts Maul in two, and his body drops down the shaft.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace

accounts.claim: Maul lives, his legs replaced by a scrap-metal body, raving in a cave on the junk world Lotho Minor.
accounts.source: Brothers (episode)

accounts.claim: Talzin restores his mind and gives him new legs.
accounts.source: Revenge (episode)

accounts.claim: Maul finally dies at Obi-Wan's hand on Tatooine in 2 BBY.
accounts.source: Twin Suns (episode)

anomalies.resolution: Settled in canon: Maul lives from Naboo until Obi-Wan kills him on Tatooine in 2 BBY. Nothing in the films contradicts it, and the films never mention it either.
sources: Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace

anomalies.title: Two founding years for the Separatists
anomalies.summary: Dooku's Raxus Address in 24 BBY starts the secession, and Rise of the Separatists treats it as the Confederacy's creation. Attack of the Clones shows the trade guilds and corporations joining at Geonosis in 22 BBY, which other works treat as the formal founding. Wookieepedia's timeline lists both as the start.

accounts.claim: Dooku's address from Raxus launches the Confederacy two years before the war.
accounts.source: Rise of the Separatists

accounts.claim: The commerce guilds and corporations pledge their armies to Dooku at Geonosis on the eve of war.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones

accounts.claim: The Confederacy is created in 24 BBY and officially founded in 22 BBY.
accounts.source: Wookieepedia's Confederacy article

anomalies.resolution: Read as stages: 24 BBY for the political secession, 22 BBY for the formal pact with the corporate backers. The chronicle anchors the founding to the Raxus Address.
sources: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones

anomalies.title: Was it Qui-Gon on Mortis?
anomalies.summary: On Mortis, Obi-Wan and then Anakin meet a figure of the late Qui-Gon, who talks with them about the Chosen One. Back at the Temple, Obi-Wan tells the Council it was an illusion drawn from their memories. The reference works disagree with each other, and with him, about what it was.

accounts.claim: It truly was Qui-Gon who appeared to them.
accounts.source: Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition

accounts.claim: It was a vision that they wrongly took for a real manifestation.
accounts.source: Qui-Gon Jinn Biography Gallery, Databank

accounts.claim: The figure was an illusion the Mortis beings built from our memories.
accounts.source: Obi-Wan Kenobi, Voices

accounts.claim: Anakin is not so sure, and doubts the teaching that no one keeps their identity after death.
accounts.source: Voices

anomalies.resolution: Unsettled. Wookieepedia's Qui-Gon article follows the Visual Dictionary; its Force spirit article follows the Databank's vision. Qui-Gon's voice later reaching Yoda favors a real presence, but not on Mortis itself.
sources: Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition

anomalies.title: The chip Fives found, filed away
anomalies.summary: When the clone Tup kills his Jedi general, the Kaminoans blame a virus. His friend Fives digs deeper, learns every clone carries a chip that will make him kill Jedi, and is framed for attacking the Chancellor and shot. The Council accepts a finding of one defective chip, and the file sits until Order 66.

accounts.claim: Tup's breakdown may be a virus, so Fives must be kept in quarantine.
accounts.source: Nala Se, Conspiracy

accounts.claim: Every clone carries a chip that will turn him on the Jedi, and the Chancellor is behind it.
accounts.source: Fives, Orders (episode)

accounts.claim: Fives tried to assassinate the Chancellor and had to be stopped.
accounts.source: The Republic's account, Orders (episode)

accounts.claim: One trooper's chip was found defective, and both the Council and a Senate panel signed off on that finding.
accounts.source: Nala Se's recorded report, Shattered

anomalies.resolution: The record survives, filed as a single faulty chip. During Order 66 Ahsoka pulls Fives's file and Rex's report from the Republic's computer and uses them to free Rex, too late for anyone else.

anomalies.title: Obi-Wan's certain point of view
anomalies.summary: Luke grows up with two false stories about his father. Owen says he was a navigator on a spice freighter; Obi-Wan says Vader betrayed and murdered him. Vader tells Luke the truth at Cloud City. Obi-Wan's spirit then defends his version: Anakin was destroyed when he became Vader, so it was true from a certain point of view.

accounts.claim: Luke's father was a navigator on a spice freighter.
accounts.source: Owen Lars, Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope

accounts.claim: Vader, a pupil turned to evil, betrayed and murdered Luke's father.
accounts.source: Obi-Wan Kenobi, Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope

accounts.claim: Vader is Luke's father.
accounts.source: Darth Vader, Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back

accounts.claim: Anakin ceased to be when he became Vader, so the story was true from a certain point of view.
accounts.source: Obi-Wan Kenobi's spirit, Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

anomalies.resolution: Vader's account is the fact, and Yoda confirms it before he dies. Obi-Wan's defense rests on what counts as the man: in his telling, Anakin died when Vader was born.
sources: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith
Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope
Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back
Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

anomalies.title: Order 66 recast as a Jedi rebellion
anomalies.summary: When four Jedi Masters try to arrest him, Palpatine survives, calls it an attempted coup, and orders the clones to execute every Jedi. Before the Senate he names it the Jedi rebellion and proclaims the Empire to applause. Later Imperial accounts say the Jedi caused the war, and Empire Day celebrates the galaxy's salvation.

accounts.claim: The Jedi tried to overthrow the Senate and kill him; the survivors will be hunted down.
accounts.source: Palpatine, Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith

accounts.claim: The Jedi were behind the Separatists and plotted to take the Republic from within.
accounts.source: Imperial claims, Darth Vader (2017) 1; Crimson Reign 3

accounts.claim: Empire Day marks the day the Emperor ended the Clone Wars and saved the galaxy.
accounts.source: Imperial HoloNet, Ezra's Duel with Danger

accounts.claim: The clones kill their generals on Palpatine's word, and Vader leads the killing in the Temple.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith

anomalies.resolution: The lie holds inside the story for a generation. The works leave no doubt that Order 66 was built into the clones from the start and waited only for Palpatine's command.
sources: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith

anomalies.title: How Padmé died, and who was told
anomalies.summary: On Polis Massa the medical droids find Padmé physically sound but losing the will to live; she dies after the twins are born. Palpatine tells the newly armored Vader that he killed her in his anger. At her funeral her body is made to look still pregnant, so the galaxy never learns the children lived.

accounts.claim: Medically she is healthy but has lost the will to live; she dies after giving birth to twins.
accounts.source: Medical droid, Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith

accounts.claim: Vader killed her himself, in his anger on Mustafar.
accounts.source: Palpatine, Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith

accounts.claim: The mortician makes her body appear still pregnant, hiding that the twins survived.
accounts.source: Darth Vader (2015) 10

accounts.claim: A record on Polis Massa holds her last words: that good remained in him.
accounts.source: Darth Vader (2020) 5

anomalies.resolution: The film leaves room for both the droid and Palpatine: Vader's attack and her despair together bring her death. Palpatine's version is the one Vader lives with, and the twins' secret holds until Aphra's droid tortures the mortician.
sources: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith

anomalies.title: What Leia remembers of her mother
anomalies.summary: On Endor, Leia tells Luke she remembers her real mother a little: very beautiful, kind, but sad. Revenge of the Sith, made twenty-two years later, has Padmé die minutes after the twins are born. Since then readers have argued whether Leia meant Padmé or her adoptive mother Breha, and how a newborn could remember either.

accounts.claim: Leia recalls her real mother as beautiful, kind but sad; she died when Leia was very young.
accounts.source: Leia Organa, Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

accounts.claim: Padmé dies on Polis Massa moments after giving birth.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith

accounts.claim: He wanted one twin to remember their mother and went back and forth over whether it should be Leia.
accounts.source: George Lucas

accounts.claim: Leia is remembering Padmé.
accounts.source: StarWars.com Q&A, of uncertain standing

anomalies.resolution: Wookieepedia reads it as images and feelings of Padmé that Leia carried through the Force and Luke did not. The line was never changed, and no film explains it.
sources: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith
Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

anomalies.title: Threepio forgets; Artoo remembers
anomalies.summary: As the Clone Wars end, Bail Organa has C-3PO's mind wiped so he cannot give away the twins or their parents; R2-D2 is left as he is. Nineteen years later Obi-Wan tells Luke he doesn't recall owning a droid. In 35 ABY Threepio is wiped again to read a Sith inscription, and Artoo restores him from a backup.

accounts.claim: Bail orders the protocol droid's mind wiped and leaves the astromech alone.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith

accounts.claim: Obi-Wan says he can't recall ever owning a droid.
accounts.source: Obi-Wan Kenobi, Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope

accounts.claim: Bypassing his programming erases Threepio's memory; Artoo restores it from a copy he kept.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

accounts.claim: Cad Bane has both droids wiped after scanning them for the Senate's layout.
accounts.source: Evil Plans

anomalies.resolution: After the 19 BBY wipe, Threepio meets Obi-Wan and Vader in A New Hope as strangers. Artoo, spared that day, keeps the whole record, and the films never show him telling it.
sources: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith
Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope
Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

anomalies.title: The Empire writes the Jedi out
anomalies.summary: After Order 66 the Empire hunts more than the survivors. Inquisitors destroy what Jedi records and relics they find, the Temple is stripped of its art and made the Emperor's palace, and the Order is taught as traitors. Two decades on, the Jedi way is called a hokey religion; by 34 ABY, Luke is thought a myth.

accounts.claim: Every mosaic, tapestry and statue of the Order is removed from the Temple, now the Imperial Palace.
accounts.source: Tarkin (novel)

accounts.claim: Palpatine called the Jedi traitors who used their powers to undermine democracy and cause the war.
accounts.source: The Archivist, Crimson Reign 3

accounts.claim: The Force is a hokey religion; an admiral mocks Vader's sad devotion to it.
accounts.source: Han Solo and Admiral Motti, Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope

accounts.claim: Rey thought Luke Skywalker was a myth; Han tells her the Jedi were real.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens

anomalies.resolution: Broad but incomplete. Jocasta Nu's hidden cache, Obi-Wan's journal and scattered holocrons survive, and Luke spends years recovering what he can. How much ordinary people remember differs from one work to the next.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope
Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens

anomalies.title: Two massacres on Ghorman
anomalies.summary: The old Expanded Universe put the Ghorman Massacre in the first days of the Empire: Tarkin landing his warship on protesters who blocked the pad. Andor makes the Ghorman Massacre the 2 BBY killing in Palmo, a trap the ISB spends years building, and keeps the older story as a separate atrocity, the Tarkin Massacre of 19 BBY.

accounts.claim: Shortly after the Empire is declared, Tarkin sets his ship down on Ghorman protesters, killing hundreds; the atrocity turns Bail Organa toward rebellion.
accounts.source: The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook (Legends)

accounts.claim: The Ghorman Massacre is the Empire's 2 BBY slaughter of protesters in Palmo, provoked by the ISB to justify seizing the planet.
accounts.source: Who Are You?

accounts.claim: Tarkin's landing on the protesters still happened, as the Tarkin Massacre of 19 BBY.
accounts.source: Ever Been to Ghorman?

anomalies.resolution: Canon keeps both events: the Tarkin Massacre in 19 BBY and the Ghorman Massacre in 2 BBY. The Legends account now describes the first one, under a new name.

anomalies.title: The storm that sank Tipoca City
anomalies.summary: Imperial Venators bombard Tipoca City to end Kaminoan cloning, and Vice Admiral Rampart tells the Senate a cataclysmic storm sank it. A year later Senator Chuchi plays his own ships' logs to the chamber. Mas Amedda then condemns Rampart as a lone war criminal, though Rampart protests he followed orders; Tarkin had authorized the attack.

accounts.claim: A cataclysmic storm devastated Kamino, so the Empire needs a new, recruited army.
accounts.source: Rampart and his Senate allies, The Clone Conspiracy

accounts.claim: Rampart's own Venators destroyed the city, as his command log shows.
accounts.source: Senator Riyo Chuchi, Truth and Consequences

accounts.claim: Rampart acted alone, for his own ends, and is arrested for war crimes.
accounts.source: Mas Amedda, Truth and Consequences

accounts.claim: He was only following orders.
accounts.source: Rampart, Truth and Consequences

anomalies.resolution: The storm story collapses, but a second story takes its place: Rampart alone is blamed, and the orders above him are never aired. The recruitment bill he championed goes forward.

anomalies.title: Did Qui-Gon speak to Obi-Wan before 9 BBY?
anomalies.summary: In the short story Time of Death, the dying Obi-Wan remembers Qui-Gon's voice waking him on Tatooine to warn that young Luke is in danger, during the raid on the Lars farm. The Obi-Wan Kenobi series, made later, has Obi-Wan calling for his old master without answer until Qui-Gon finally appears in 9 BBY.

accounts.claim: Qui-Gon's voice rouses Obi-Wan in the night to say Luke is in danger.
accounts.source: Time of Death

accounts.claim: Obi-Wan's pleas to Qui-Gon go unanswered until he appears after the rematch with Vader.
accounts.source: Part VI

accounts.claim: He doesn't know whether the story was retconned or will be changed, and doesn't worry about it.
accounts.source: Cavan Scott, author of Time of Death (2026)

anomalies.resolution: The series is the later and more prominent work, and the archive follows it for 9 BBY. Time of Death has not been revised, and its author leaves its status open.
sources: From a Certain Point of View

anomalies.title: The Kessel Run in less than twelve parsecs
anomalies.summary: Han sells the Falcon to Obi-Wan as the ship that made the Kessel Run in less than twelve parsecs, which measures distance, not time. The run itself, flown years earlier, shows what he meant: a shorter and more dangerous path through the Maelstrom, and a figure he rounds in his own favour.

accounts.claim: The Falcon is the ship that made the Kessel Run in less than twelve parsecs.
accounts.source: Han Solo, Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope

accounts.claim: Han takes the Falcon through the Akkadese Maelstrom and comes out a little over twelve parsecs; when Chewbacca corrects his boast, Han says it is twelve if you round down.
accounts.source: Solo: A Star Wars Story

anomalies.resolution: Solo makes the old line a claim about distance: the Kessel Run is a route of about twenty parsecs, and Han's shortcut brings it to a little over twelve. Less than twelve is the salesman's figure.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope

anomalies.title: Where the first Death Star was finished
anomalies.summary: The battle station begins in orbit over Geonosis and ends at Scarif, but the sources disagree on when it moves. Wookieepedia's timeline, summarizing the novel Tarkin, has it leave Geonosis for deep space by 14 BBY. Rogue One reference material keeps it over Geonosis until Saw Gerrera gets too close, around 9 BBY.

accounts.claim: The station leaves Geonosis orbit for deep space in 14 BBY.
accounts.source: Wookieepedia's timeline, summarizing Tarkin (novel)

accounts.claim: After Saw Gerrera nearly finds it, the Empire moves the station from Geonosis to Scarif for its final stages.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide

anomalies.resolution: Wookieepedia's Death Star article follows the Rogue One material, with the move near 9 BBY; the timeline entry is the outlier. The chronicle follows the article.
sources: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide

anomalies.title: Ghorman: the Empire's story and Mon Mothma's
anomalies.summary: The Empire wants Ghorman's kalkite for the Death Star. The ISB spends years painting the Ghor as dangerous, arms their resistance through an informer, and provokes troops into firing on a peaceful crowd in Palmo Plaza. In the Senate the slaughter is spun as a savage uprising and Ghorman's senator is arrested. Mon Mothma calls it genocide.

accounts.claim: Ghorman's kalkite is needed, and a campaign against the Ghor will justify seizing it.
accounts.source: Director Krennic, One Year Later

accounts.claim: Ghorman's provocations brought on a savage attack that had to be put down.
accounts.source: Senator Den Gane, Welcome to the Rebellion

accounts.claim: The massacre was genocide, and the Emperor is a lying executioner.
accounts.source: Mon Mothma, Welcome to the Rebellion

accounts.claim: Krennic uses the event to justify crushing radicals; Luthen uses it to wake the uncommitted.
accounts.source: Dan Gilroy, Andor writer

anomalies.resolution: The Imperial version rules the Senate floor, and dissent means arrest. But Mothma's speech and the massacre itself help pull the rebel cells together into the Alliance.

anomalies.title: Does Barriss Offee die?
anomalies.summary: Years after leaving the Inquisitorius, Barriss tends travelers from a camp on an icy world until the Fourth Sister finds her. The Way Out ends with the Inquisitor carrying her, gravely wounded, out of a cave. A Darth Vader magazine twice says she dies; Star Wars Insider calls her wounded; the Story Group wants it left open.

accounts.claim: The Fourth Sister impales her by accident, promises to save her, and carries her out; the episode stops there.
accounts.source: The Way Out

accounts.claim: Barriss dies in these events.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Darth Vader 68 and 78

accounts.claim: She is seriously wounded, and the Fourth Sister sets out to save her.
accounts.source: Star Wars Insider 229 and 236

accounts.claim: The Story Group asked for the magazine's death line to be cut and has not settled her fate.
accounts.source: Emily Shkoukani, Lucasfilm Story Group

anomalies.resolution: Open by the Story Group's choice. Wookieepedia sets aside the magazine's claim and gives no death date; the personnel file records her as gravely wounded.

anomalies.title: The Empire's stories for Jedha and Alderaan
anomalies.summary: The Death Star's first shot levels Jedha City, and Vader tells Krennic the station does not exist; the Senate will hear of a mining disaster. Days later Alderaan is destroyed in the open, after years in which the Empire warned that the world threatened the peace. Decades on, some still believe Jedha's official story.

accounts.claim: There is no Death Star; the Senate is told Jedha was lost in a mining disaster.
accounts.source: Darth Vader, Rogue One: A Star Wars Story

accounts.claim: By the Cold War, some say the city died in a real mining accident and the Empire only claimed it.
accounts.source: The Legends of Luke Skywalker

accounts.claim: Alderaan is a dangerous world, set against the security the Empire provides.
accounts.source: Imperial warnings, The Rebellion Begins

accounts.claim: Alderaan was probably chosen in advance for its pacifism, to show where even peaceful resistance leads.
accounts.source: Historian Beaumont Kin, Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire

anomalies.resolution: Jedha's cover story outlives the Empire; Alderaan's end is known within days through official statements and pirated news. Tarkin's stated reason, to make Leia talk, is only part of the explanation in later histories.
sources: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope
Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire

anomalies.title: The Death Star's flaw was built in
anomalies.summary: A New Hope presents the exhaust port as a weakness the rebels find by studying the stolen plans: a small shaft straight to the reactor. Rogue One, made thirty-nine years later, reveals that the engineer Galen Erso put it there on purpose, a trap hidden in the station he was forced to design, and told the Rebellion.

accounts.claim: Analysis of the plans shows a small port leading straight to the reactor; one precise hit could destroy the station.
accounts.source: General Dodonna, Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope

accounts.claim: Galen has hidden a weakness in the reactor that one shot can trigger, and tells Jyn where the plans are.
accounts.source: Galen Erso's message, Rogue One: A Star Wars Story

accounts.claim: Galen designed the exhaust port as an act of sabotage.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide

anomalies.resolution: Rogue One's answer is canon. A New Hope's scenes still stand, now read as the rebels finding a flaw that was meant to be found.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope
Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)
Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide

anomalies.title: Who shot first in the cantina?
anomalies.summary: In the 1977 film, Han shoots the bounty hunter Greedo across a cantina table and Greedo never fires. The 1997 Special Edition adds a shot from Greedo that misses at point-blank range; the 2004 release makes the shots almost simultaneous; the 2019 Disney+ release gives Greedo a last word. It is the saga's best-known revision of itself.

accounts.claim: Han fires, and Greedo never gets a shot off.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope, 1977 release

accounts.claim: Greedo fires first and misses; then Han kills him.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope, 1997 Special Edition

accounts.claim: He wanted Han to read as a cowboy defending himself, not a cold killer.
accounts.source: George Lucas

accounts.claim: Han fires before Greedo can shoot.
accounts.source: Alexandra Bracken, author of A New Hope: The Princess, the Scoundrel, and the Farm Boy

anomalies.resolution: Later releases keep a Greedo shot a split second ahead of Han's. The author of the 2015 junior novelization sides with the 1977 cut, where Han alone fires.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope
A New Hope: The Princess, the Scoundrel, and the Farm Boy

anomalies.title: The months before Yavin change year
anomalies.summary: The archive counts from the Battle of Yavin, yet the sources have moved the months just before it. Star Wars: Galactic Atlas put Rogue One and the first part of A New Hope in 0 BBY. Star Wars: Timelines and the Story Group now say no 0 BBY exists: all of that is 1 BBY, and the battle is 0.

accounts.claim: Rogue One and the events of A New Hope before the battle fall in 0 BBY.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Galactic Atlas

accounts.claim: There is no 0 BBY; those events are 1 BBY, the battle is 0, and the next year is 0 ABY.
accounts.source: Emily Shkoukani, Lucasfilm Story Group

accounts.claim: Rogue One is dated 1 BBY and A New Hope 0.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Timelines

accounts.claim: Yavin itself is year zero; nothing is dated 0 BBY.
accounts.source: Pablo Hidalgo, Lucasfilm Story Group (2025)

anomalies.resolution: The newer reckoning holds. Wookieepedia and this archive put Scarif, Alderaan and the months before Yavin in 1 BBY and the battle at 0. Star Wars 100 Objects still uses 0 BBY on one page and 1 BBY on another.
sources: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope
Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition

anomalies.title: How long Echo Base took to build
anomalies.summary: The rebels' ice base on Hoth falls in 3 ABY, but the sources disagree on when it went up. Star Wars: Complete Locations says building took about two years. Star Wars: Galactic Atlas says it was built in 3 ABY, and The Rebel Files says it was finished only weeks before the Empire found it.

accounts.claim: Building runs for roughly two years, ending at the Battle of Hoth.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)

accounts.claim: Echo Base is built in 3 ABY.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Galactic Atlas

accounts.claim: The base is completed less than a month before an Imperial probe droid finds it.
accounts.source: Star Wars: The Rebel Files

anomalies.resolution: Wookieepedia reads them together: work begins around 1 ABY and ends in 3 ABY, weeks before the battle, with the Atlas year taken as the year of completion. The chronicle uses the same span.
sources: Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back

anomalies.title: Was the second Death Star news?
anomalies.summary: In Moving Target, rebel commanders react with disbelief when Ackbar shows them Bothan footage of a new Death Star at Endor, as if hearing of it for the first time. But in the Star Wars comic, around 3 ABY, Luke has already told Mon Mothma and Ackbar that the Empire is building another one.

accounts.claim: Madine and Massa doubt the footage until Ackbar says Bothan agents took it less than a week ago.
accounts.source: Moving Target: A Princess Leia Adventure

accounts.claim: Luke tells Mon Mothma a second Death Star is under way, and she resolves that they will destroy it again.
accounts.source: Star Wars (2020) 28

accounts.claim: Bothan spies locate the station and its shield generator on Endor; many die for the information.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

anomalies.resolution: Unreconciled. The chronicle keeps both: the rebels learn of a second station in 3 ABY, and the Bothans locate it in 4 ABY. Nothing explains the commanders' surprise in Moving Target.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi
Moving Target: A Princess Leia Adventure

anomalies.title: Who fulfilled the Chosen One prophecy?
anomalies.summary: The Jedi prophecy promises one who will bring balance by destroying the Sith. Most sources credit Anakin, who kills the Emperor at Endor. But Sidious returns in 35 ABY and Rey ends him, and the people closest to the story have named Luke, Rey and even Leia instead.

accounts.claim: Anakin completed the Chosen One's destiny when he ended the rule of the Sith.
accounts.source: George Lucas; Darth Vader: Sith Lord

accounts.claim: Obi-Wan believes Vader's son is the Chosen One.
accounts.source: Obi-Wan Kenobi, Twin Suns (episode)

accounts.claim: Rey fulfils the prophecy; the one need not be a Skywalker by blood.
accounts.source: Rick Carter, The Art of Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker

accounts.claim: In Lucas's own plans for a sequel trilogy, Leia ends up being the Chosen One.
accounts.source: George Lucas

anomalies.resolution: Anakin remains the Chosen One in most sources. The Rise of Skywalker has his spirit ask Rey to restore balance as he once did, and Abrams and Terrio describe balance as something restored again and again.
sources: Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace
Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi
Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
The Art of Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: The Secrets of the Sith

anomalies.title: Palpatine's return from Endor
anomalies.summary: Return of the Jedi ends with the Emperor thrown down a reactor shaft and the station destroyed. The Rise of Skywalker brings him back on Exegol in a failing cloned body, the maker of Snoke and the voice in Kylo Ren's head. The film gives no mechanism, and later books and Wookieepedia's articles disagree on the timing.

accounts.claim: Vader hurls the Emperor down the reactor shaft, and he dies.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

accounts.claim: He lives on Exegol, made Snoke, and has been every voice Kylo Ren heard.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

accounts.claim: Falling, he sends his consciousness into a cloned body his cultists prepared on Exegol.
accounts.source: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition

accounts.claim: Some Wookieepedia articles place the transfer just before his body's destruction, others just after its death.
accounts.source: Wookieepedia, Darth Sidious and related articles

anomalies.resolution: The return is canon, and the novelization's transfer into a clone is the accepted mechanism. Whether his spirit left before or after death stays open.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi
Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition
Star Wars: The Secrets of the Sith

anomalies.title: The New Republic: 4 ABY or 5 ABY
anomalies.summary: Mon Mothma proclaims the New Republic in the months after Endor. Star Wars: On the Front Lines and Star Wars: Galactic Atlas put the founding in 4 ABY. The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary says it was officially founded twenty-nine years before the Starkiller strike, a year after Endor, in 5 ABY.

accounts.claim: The New Republic is declared in 4 ABY, soon after the Battle of Endor.
accounts.source: Star Wars: On the Front Lines; Star Wars: Galactic Atlas

accounts.claim: The New Republic is officially founded a year after Endor.
accounts.source: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

anomalies.resolution: Wookieepedia reads them as two steps: the declaration in 4 ABY, the formal founding in 5 ABY. The chronicle dates the declaration to 4 ABY.
sources: Star Wars: On the Front Lines
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

anomalies.title: The Expanded Universe becomes Legends
anomalies.summary: For decades, novels, comics and games carried the story past Return of the Jedi: Thrawn's campaign, Han and Leia's children, the Yuuzhan Vong war. On April 25, 2014, Lucasfilm set that material aside, kept only the six films and The Clone Wars, and began a new continuity. The old books stayed in print as Legends.

accounts.claim: The Expanded Universe is rebranded Legends and no longer followed; canon is the six films, The Clone Wars, and all new work.
accounts.source: Lucasfilm announcement, April 25, 2014

accounts.claim: Years after Endor, Grand Admiral Thrawn rallies the Empire's remnants against the New Republic.
accounts.source: Heir to the Empire

accounts.claim: Luke's attempt to rebuild the Jedi ends when his nephew Ben burns his academy.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi

accounts.claim: Legends stays a resource new stories can draw on; Thrawn returns in canon with a new history.
accounts.source: Thrawn (novel)

anomalies.resolution: Canon is what Lucasfilm publishes now; Legends is a closed continuity, shown in this archive as its own layer. The two share the six films and The Clone Wars, and canon borrows Legends names and events freely.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi
Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi
Star Wars: The New Jedi Order

anomalies.title: When Poe left the Spice Runners
anomalies.summary: Poe runs spice with Zorii's crew as a teenager before joining the New Republic Navy. Poe Dameron: Free Fall, which Star Wars: Timelines dates to 18–19 ABY, has him quit after a summit on Kijimi. The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary says he left eleven years before the Starkiller strike, in 23 ABY.

accounts.claim: Poe breaks with the Spice Runners after defying Zeva Bliss at the Kijimi summit.
accounts.source: Poe Dameron: Free Fall

accounts.claim: The novel's events run from 18 to 19 ABY.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Timelines

accounts.claim: Poe left the Spice Runners eleven years before the Starkiller Incident.
accounts.source: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

anomalies.resolution: Unresolved: four years separate the two. The chronicle follows the novel's dating, 19 ABY.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

anomalies.title: Rey's parents: nobodies, then Palpatines
anomalies.summary: In The Last Jedi, Kylo Ren tells Rey her parents were junk traders who sold her for drink and lie in a pauper's grave, and she admits she knew. The Rise of Skywalker makes her father a clone son of Palpatine, and has her parents hide her on Jakku to protect her and die refusing to give her up.

accounts.claim: Her parents were nobodies: junk traders who sold her off and died on Jakku.
accounts.source: Kylo Ren, Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi

accounts.claim: She is Palpatine's granddaughter; her parents hid her from him and were killed for it.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

accounts.claim: The Last Jedi's answer was the hardest thing she could hear: her parents were no one special.

accounts.claim: They were junk traders, and the new film did not contradict that; it made the news worse.

anomalies.resolution: The later film governs. Shadow of the Sith names them Dathan and Miramir, who chose to live as junk traders to stay hidden. Kylo's 'sold her for drinking money' is Rey's fear, not what happened.

anomalies.title: The night Luke's temple burned
anomalies.summary: The Last Jedi tells the fall of Luke's academy three times. Luke first says Ben simply turned on him. Ben says he woke with his uncle's lit saber above him. Luke then admits he did ignite it, for a moment, over his sleeping nephew, before shame caught up with him.

accounts.claim: Luke saw darkness growing in Ben, and Ben turned on him and destroyed it all.
accounts.source: Luke Skywalker, first telling, Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi

accounts.claim: His uncle sensed his power, feared it, and came to kill him in his sleep.
accounts.source: Ben Solo, Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi

accounts.claim: For one instinctive moment Luke drew his saber to stop what he saw coming, then was ashamed; Ben woke.
accounts.source: Luke Skywalker, second telling, Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi

accounts.claim: Ben tells the surviving students that Luke tried to murder him and is now dead.
accounts.source: The Rise of Kylo Ren 1

anomalies.resolution: Luke's second telling stands as the true one. Ben's account is how it looked to him, and The Rise of Kylo Ren shows him repeating it to the students who survived.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi
Star Wars: The Last Jedi: A Junior Novel
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

anomalies.title: The First Order's version of events
anomalies.summary: The First Order presents itself as the Empire's rightful heir and the New Republic as illegitimate, and raises its stormtroopers on a slanted history. Before Starkiller fires, Hux tells the troops the Republic deceives the galaxy and quietly backs the Resistance. On the Colossus it pays pirates to raid the station until its captain accepts protection.

accounts.claim: The Republic lies to the galaxy and secretly supports the treacherous Resistance; today it ends.
accounts.source: General Hux, Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens

accounts.claim: Stormtroopers learn a pro-Imperial history, which FN-2187 doubts.
accounts.source: Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary

accounts.claim: The First Order is the Empire's lawful successor, and the New Republic is not a legitimate government.
accounts.source: First Order propaganda, Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy

accounts.claim: The pirates raiding the Colossus are hired by the First Order to make the station need its protection.
accounts.source: The High Tower

anomalies.resolution: Other works show a Republic that let the Resistance operate but refused to go to war with the Order, so Hux's charge holds only in part. The First Order's history lessons are never shown in full.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens
Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary
Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy

anomalies.title: Ahsoka's voice among the dead Jedi
anomalies.summary: When Rey faces Palpatine on Exegol, the voices of past Jedi rise to support her, and Ahsoka Tano's is among them. No work shows Ahsoka dead by then; the last on record, she is alive in 9 ABY. Some of the other speakers, such as Mace Windu, never learned to return as spirits at all.

accounts.claim: Ahsoka's voice joins the Jedi who tell Rey to rise.
accounts.source: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

accounts.claim: Ahsoka is alive in 9 ABY, stranded on Peridea with Anakin's spirit watching over her.
accounts.source: Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord

accounts.claim: Jedi who never learned the technique, like Mace Windu, can still be heard as voices after death.
accounts.source: Wookieepedia's Force spirit article, reading The Rise of Skywalker

anomalies.resolution: Unexplained. Wookieepedia lists her voice without dating her death, and no source says whether she had died by 35 ABY or spoke to Rey some other way.

personnel.summary: Taken from Dathomir to be Sidious's apprentice, Darth Maul kills Qui-Gon Jinn on Naboo and is cut in half by Obi-Wan Kenobi. Restored by his mother Talzin, he seizes Mandalore at the head of a crime alliance, loses it as the Republic falls, and rules the underworld from hiding. His hunt for Obi-Wan ends in death on Tatooine.

He leads the Separatists through the Clone Wars, betraying his own disciples at his master's word, until Anakin Skywalker beheads him at Palpatine's urging.

He leads the Jedi at Geonosis and fights through the Clone Wars, freeing Ryloth. When he moves to arrest Palpatine as a Sith Lord, Anakin Skywalker takes Palpatine's side and Mace is killed.

Rescued from Vader through the World Between Worlds, she later hunts for Ezra Bridger and Thrawn, training Sabine Wren.
